source_name: ČNB – OAM historical archive of regulated information filed before 31 July 2009
why_relevant: Separate legacy store for regulated information submitted before 31 July 2009. Essential for long-run time series on Czech bank/payments issuers (pre-crisis disclosure history) which the current OAM does not contain.

source_name: ČNB – Přehled odkazů na webové stránky bank obsahující povinně uveřejňované informace
why_relevant: The single highest-leverage pointer for this entire workstream: the regulator itself maintains the authoritative, curated list of every licensed Czech bank's mandatory-disclosure URL. One fetch resolved the correct disclosure page for Raiffeisenbank, MONETA, Air Bank, Fio, Banka CREDITAS, Trinity Bank, Max banka and Partners Banka simultaneously — eliminating guesswork about which of a bank's many pages is the statutory one. It doubles as a change-detector: entries appearing or disappearing signal licence grants, mergers and wind-downs. Roughly two dozen banks are listed, so it also defines the universe boundary for the domestic-licence cohort.

source_name: ČNB – Seznam emitentů s povolením pro krytý blok a krytých dluhopisů (covered bond issuers list, PDF)
why_relevant: Bank-specific: enumerates which Czech banks hold a ČNB permission for a cover pool (krytý blok) and the covered bonds (hypoteční zástavní listy / kryté dluhopisy) issued under it. Directly identifies the subset of banks with structured funding programmes and therefore with the richest recurring investor-relations and cover-pool disclosure output.

source_name: BCPP Prime Market share list (Prime Market — akcie)
why_relevant: Authoritative roster of the strictest-disclosure regulated segment. As observed it carries 12 issues, of which three are banks with full CZ/EU disclosure duty: ERSTE GROUP BANK (AT0000652011), KOMERČNÍ BANKA (CZ0008019106), MONETA MONEY BANK (CZ0008040318); VIG (AT0000908504) adds insurance/bancassurance exposure. This list is the cheapest reliable way to know which CZ-listed banks currently carry Prime-level disclosure duty and to detect additions/removals.

source_name: BCPP Standard Market share list — includes SAB FINANCE (FX/cross-border payments)
why_relevant: Regulated market for other equity issues. As observed it carries 8 issues including SAB FINANCE a.s. (CZ0009009940) — a licensed Czech FX/payment-services provider and the closest thing on the regulated CZ market to a listed pure payments company — plus RMS MEZZANINE (CS0008416251), a financial/investment vehicle. This makes the Standard Market list the main pointer to non-bank financial issuers with statutory disclosure duty.

source_name: BCPP Free Market share list (Volný trh) — foreign bank and payment issuers dual-listed in Prague
why_relevant: Unregulated segment used mainly for dual listings; it is where the Prague venue carries the largest cluster of banking/payments names: WAG PAYMENT SOLUTIONS (Eurowag, GB00BLGXWY71 — commercial road-transport payments), DEUTSCHE BANK (DE0005140008), OTP BANK (HU0000061726), PKO BANK POLSKI (PLPKO0000016), RBI / Raiffeisen Bank International (AT0000606306), UNIQA INSURANCE (AT0000821103), ATS (AT0000969985). Useful as a CEE-peer watchlist anchored to a Czech venue, and the only Prague-listed pure payments name found in this scan.

source_name: BCPP START Market issuer list (trh START)
why_relevant: The SME/growth segment (MTF) open only to Czech and Slovak companies — the venue where a small Czech fintech would most plausibly list, and the reason this cell exists as a fintech early-warning tripwire. Observed roster: BEZVAVLASY, EMAN (CZ0009009718 — IT/software house that builds banking and mobility apps), FILLAMENTUM, FIXED.ZONE, HARDWARIO, M&T 1997, M2C, MMCITÉ, PILULKA LÉKÁRNY, PRABOS PLUS. No pure payments/fintech issuer was present at scan time, but the list must be diffed because admission requires only a CEO decision, so new names can appear between quarterly auctions.

source_name: CzechStartups.gov.cz (CzechInvest startup ecosystem portal)
why_relevant: Official state startup-ecosystem platform under CzechInvest (the old czechstartups.org now 301-redirects here). It exposes structured directories — startups at /startup-ekosystem/startupy/, investors at /startup-ekosystem/investori/, ecosystem data at /startup-data/ and support programmes at /programy/ — and advertises 44 investors, 208 startup infrastructures and 300 events per year. As a pointer this is the state-sanctioned counterpart to the association member list: it names the investors whose portfolio announcements the media in this cell will report.

source_name: Asociace pro elektronickou komerci (APEK) — Seznam členů
why_relevant: APEK's member directory explicitly states 570 listed members across 64 paginated pages, each with its own detail URL. This is by a wide margin the largest single enumeration found in this cell and the definitive map of the Czech e-commerce merchant and vendor base — the demand side for acquiring, payment gateways, BNPL and POS services. Each member detail page is a stable per-company URL, making the directory usable as a persistent company registry, not just a list.

source_name: ČBA — Slovník bankovních pojmů (Czech banking terminology glossary)
why_relevant: The bulk of ČBA's sitemap (roughly 2,100 of 2,838 URLs) is a one-term-per-page Czech banking glossary covering everything from 'zúčtovací systém' and 'zaknihovaný cenný papír' to 'zpráva auditora' and 'zlatá kreditní karta'. For a source-scouting workstream this is a ready-made, authoritative cs<->en terminology corpus for building the local-language query glossary that all other cells depend on — an indirect but high-leverage asset.

source_name: Česká bankovní asociace (ČBA) — Členové / Members registry
why_relevant: Server-rendered roster of ČBA member banks — the cheapest near-complete enumeration of licensed banks and foreign bank branches operating in CZ, including building societies (ČSOB Stavební spořitelna, Modrá pyramida, Raiffeisen stavební spořitelna, Stavební spořitelna ČS) and state banks (ČEB, Národní rozvojová banka). Observed ~33 entries incl. Air Bank, AS Inbank odštěpný závod, Banka CREDITAS, Bank of China (CEE), BNP Paribas pobočka, Citibank Europe, COMMERZBANK pobočka Praha, Česká spořitelna, ČSOB, Deutsche Bank Filiale Prag, Fio banka, HSBC Continental Europe, ICBC Prague Branch, ING Bank N.V., J&T BANKA, Komerční banka, mBank organizační složka, MONETA Money Bank, Oberbank AG, Partners Banka, PKO BP Czech Branch, PPF banka, Raiffeisenbank, TRINITY BANK, UniCredit Bank CZ&SK, VÚB pobočka Praha. Each name is a seed for A1 disclosure/IR/annual-report tracking. An English mirror exists at /about-us/members.

source_name: Česká leasingová a finanční asociace (ČLFA) — Členské společnosti
why_relevant: ČLFA is the Czech leasing and consumer-finance association; its member-company page is the standard enumeration of leasing companies, non-bank consumer lenders and factoring providers operating in CZ — the segment that sits outside the bank list but competes directly with bank lending. Essential complement to the ČBA roster for full coverage of Czech credit provision.

source_name: Asociace pro kapitálový trh ČR (AKAT) — Členové asociace
why_relevant: AKAT is the Czech capital-market/asset-management association, splitting its roster into 'Řádní členové' and 'Přidružení členové'. Its own press release notes the association passed 100 members and marked 30 years. Members are the asset managers, fund distributors and custodians attached to Czech banking groups (most large Czech banks run a captive investment company), so this roster completes the picture of bank-affiliated entities that publish their own disclosures.

source_name: Syncordis (Temenos implementation partner) — snowballed actor, delivery-side channel
why_relevant: Snowballed directly from the verified Komerční banka press release, which names Syncordis as the implementation partner that delivered the Temenos Transact go-live in under 12 months. Implementation and SI partners are a systematically under-watched channel: they publish project detail, headcount and phase-completion news that the software vendor and the bank both omit, and the partner directory itself expands the actor map (SIs, regional resellers) for every vendor in this cell. The named partner is the concrete lead; the vendor partner directory is the reusable pointer.

entity_name: Česká fintech asociace / Czech Fintech Association
source_name: Česká fintech asociace / Czech Fintech Association (ČEFTAS) — Členové
why_relevant: ČEFTAS (founded 2016) is the Czech fintech industry body. Its members page distinguishes 'řádní členové' (full members offering fintech solutions) from 'přidružení členové' (ecosystem supporters), and also lists partner organisations and media/conference partners — three separate enumerations in one page. This is the primary map of the Czech fintech actor set, which is otherwise poorly covered by bank-centric registries. Leadership observed to include executives from Twisto, EasyChange Group and Budget Bakers; the association itself is a member of AMSP ČR, the Czech Chamber of Commerce and the European Digital Finance Association.

entity_name: Česká fintech asociace / Czech Fintech Association
source_name: Česká fintech asociace — Studie českého fintechu (sector study)
why_relevant: A recurring sector study quantifying Czech fintech employment and economic contribution — the project page cites 6,394 people employed including 1,603 foreigners, and public-revenue contribution figures. A companion CzechTrade export brochure (https://czechfintech.cz/project/10647/) describes Czech fintech as a sector with 'more than 200 active firms'. Together these give a defensible denominator for the sector and a second, larger company list beyond the 80+ members.

source_name: CardMag (cardmag.cz) – Czech payment-cards and self-service trade magazine with PDF archive
why_relevant: Specialist Czech trade title for the cards/ATM/self-service industry with a downloadable back-issue archive. Trade press of this kind is where deployer network deals, ATM vendor wins, CIT contracts and fleet numbers get named before (or instead of) appearing in any formal disclosure, and the archive gives a long time series for reconstructing how the Czech ATM estate and its outsourcing model evolved. Primary use is as a snowballing pointer to actors, product names and events.

source_name: Aricoma — Our customers, Banks & Insurance filter
why_relevant: Aricoma (KKCG technology division, ~EUR 500m revenue, 6000+ staff) publishes a filterable customer wall with an explicit 'Banks and Insurance Companies' branch. Named financial customers observed: CSOB Group, Ceska sporitelna, Raiffeisenbank, ING Management Services, Citibank, plus Kooperativa, UNIQA, Simplea, Home Credit, Broker Consulting and SATUM. For the largest Czech integrator this customer wall is the only systematic public statement of which banks it serves, and Aricoma is a roll-up so the wall changes as it acquires.

source_name: ATM location directories and POI datasets (banky.cz, Mapy.com/OSM, Firmy.cz)
why_relevant: The only practical bottom-up way to size and profile the Czech ATM estate by operator, since neither ČNB (bank-operated only) nor SBK (stale) publishes a deployer-level breakdown. banky.cz maintains per-bank ATM listings with addresses; Mapy.com and Firmy.cz carry large numbers of individually tagged 'Bankomat Euronet' and bank ATM POIs (including OSM-sourced entries), which supports operator-mix and regional-density estimates and detects new deployments and removals over time.

source_name: Czech company-data aggregators (Chytrý rejstřík, Finmag rejstřík, Podnikatel.cz rejstřík, Měšec rejstřík firem, Živéfirmy)
why_relevant: Fast triage layer over the register: pre-parsed revenue bands, headcount, ownership chains and document counts without pulling PDFs. Confirmed for Euronet Services: revenue band 300–500 mil. Kč (ČSÚ, 2024), 10–19 employees, 100% owned by EFT Services Holding B.V. (Amsterdam) since June 2015, 56 documents in Sbírka listin, plus counts of register changes and public contracts. The tiny headcount against a 300–500m CZK revenue is itself a finding — it evidences how far the Czech ATM estate is operationally outsourced to CIT partners.

source_name: ICZ Group — Reference (incl. CEBIS for Ceska exportni banka)
why_relevant: ICZ's Czech-language reference section carries a filterable 'Bankovnictvi' / 'Pojistovnictvi' vertical. The concrete banking reference observed is CEBIS, a bespoke commercial-case origination and approval system for CEB (Ceska exportni banka) covering loans, guarantees, purchased receivables and syndicated/club deals — a rare public description of an origination platform at a state-owned Czech bank. Adjacent insurance/pension references (Dovera, VsZP, Union, STABILITA) map ICZ's document-management franchise across CZ/SK financial institutions.

source_name: Monet+ — Reference (Czech-language client case studies)
why_relevant: Monet+ (Zlin-Stipa) is the Czech specialist in banking digital identity (ProID) and card/transit payment acceptance (Switchio). Its Czech-language reference list explicitly names CSOB (EMV card acceptance in public transport), Ceska sporitelna (securing Servis24/Business24 internet banking; PKI smartcard network access) and Air Bank (secure internet-banking access). These are concrete, dated public traces of security and payment-acceptance decisions inside private Czech banks that appear nowhere else.

source_name: Shoptet Doplňky – Platby category (BNPL/instalment addon catalogue)
why_relevant: The single best pointer source found for this cell. Shoptet is the dominant Czech e-shop SaaS platform and its addon marketplace (403 addons at time of fetch) enumerates, in one place, every payment and deferred-payment provider competing for Czech checkouts: Shoptet Pay, Shoptet Boost (financing), PayPal, Cofidis iPlatba, GoPay+, Comgate, Lemonero (working capital), ThePay, Pays, HomeCredit, PlatímPak, Barion, ESSOX Payments, Skip Pay, Global Payments 2.0, Twisto Pay+, Cofidis Pay Na splátky, Inbank, Smable, Pluxee Flexi, Cashbot Pay, Skip Pay PREMIUM, PayU PREMIUM, Pluxee Gastro. It surfaced three actors absent from the seed brief (PlatímPak, Inbank, Cashbot Pay) and distinguishes standard vs PREMIUM tiers, which is itself a commercial signal.

source_name: UniCredit — 'Financial Reports from our Countries' index
why_relevant: Group-maintained index that should link each country legal entity's statutory reporting, including UniCredit Bank Czech Republic and Slovakia. If it resolves, it is a maintained pointer that survives local-site restructures — a durable discovery anchor rather than a data source.

source_name: ČTK services hub (Infobanka, ČTK Connect, News Select, Fotobanka)
why_relevant: Catalogue of the national agency's commercial products, which is where the deep, licensable archive lives: Infobanka (news database and archive), ČTK Connect (PR distribution and events), News Select (mobile news app), PressCentrum ČTK (press-conference venue — a useful signal of where Czech financial announcements are physically staged), Fotobanka/Videobanka. Infobanka is the route to historical full-text agency coverage that is not on the free web.

source_name: Protext submission/client portal (protext.ctk.cz)
why_relevant: The client-facing side of the ČTK wire. Documents how Czech corporate announcements physically enter the media system: service running since 1999, distribution to 27 Czech news portals and media in nearly 180 countries, guaranteed publication within 4 hours (usually under 2), category targeting, premium portal placement, and monitoring reports at 2h and 48h after publication. Registration is free and one-off submission without registration is possible — which explains why very small payment institutions and fintechs appear on the wire without any newsroom of their own. Useful for modelling distribution latency and for enumerating the downstream mirror portals.

source_name: Acquiring Day — Czech acquiring industry conference
why_relevant: A conference dedicated specifically to card acquiring in the Czech/CEE market, run from the SBK/CardMag stable. Agendas and speaker lists are a compact, self-updating actor map of who currently matters in Czech acquiring and processing — including vendors and processors that never issue press releases. Historical programme PDFs are hosted on the SBK site.

source_name: APRA – Asociace public relations (Czech PR agency association) member directory
why_relevant: Voluntary association of PR agencies operating in the Czech Republic, founded 1995, with a public directory of 26+ member agencies. Snowballing the member list yields the agencies whose client rosters and case studies name Czech banks, insurers and payment providers — an indirect but durable pointer to who announces what, and often to campaign material not present on corporate sites.

source_name: Banka roku (BOY AWARDS)
why_relevant: The 24-year-running Czech 'Bank of the Year' competition, organised by BOY AWARDS a.s. (Karolinska 661/4, 186 00 Praha 8, IC 04797345) with Mastercard as title sponsor. The 2025 edition was the 24th; Ceska sporitelna took the main bank award and Kooperativa the insurance category. Category evolution is itself a market signal - recent additions include 'Mobilni aplikace roku' (Mobile App of the Year) and 'Developerska banka roku', which tells you where competitive attention has shifted. 'Predchozi rocniky' archives past results, giving a ~24-year panel of Czech bank competitive standing that is fully external to bank self-disclosure.

source_name: Card Forum — cardforum.cz
why_relevant: The second event property in the Czech card ecosystem, complementing Acquiring Day with broader card/issuing coverage. Same value proposition: programme and speaker lists reveal the current roster of Czech processors, acquirers and their bank counterparties, and flag emerging vendors before they appear in trade press.

source_name: Czech cards & payments event circuit (Card Forum, Card Session, Prague Payments Week, Acquiring Day)
why_relevant: The SBK ecosystem runs a cluster of recurring industry events — Card Forum, Card Session, Prague Payments Week, Acquiring Day, plus the Contactless Hockey / Winter Classic sponsor activations. Conference agendas and speaker lists are among the cheapest ways to learn which executives own which payments initiatives, which vendors are selling into Czech banks, and what roadmap items get disclosed off the record before they reach an annual report. Treat as a pointer into people and vendors rather than a data source.

source_name: Družstevnízáložny.cz / Fintimes.cz / Peníze.cz – přehledy družstevních záložen a stavebních spořitelen
why_relevant: Third-party directories that enumerate CZ credit unions and building societies with profile pages, and that surfaced entities and historical names (WPB Capital, Prague Credit Union, DZ NOVA, Moravský peněžní ústav lineage) not visible on ČNB's current index of six active credit unions. Useful strictly as a snowballing aid for historical entity names and for cross-checking that the regulator-derived list is complete; every fact taken from here must be re-verified against JERRS or Sbírka listin.

source_name: European e-Justice Portal — Business Registers Interconnection (BRIS)
why_relevant: EU-level search across national business registers, including the Czech one. Its value for this cell is cross-border: when a CZ payment institution or processor is a subsidiary of a Slovak, Austrian, German or Polish parent, BRIS lets you follow the chain into the parent's home register (and its filings) without knowing each national portal.

source_name: ICT UNIE — member register of Czech IT and electronic-communications firms
why_relevant: Czech ICT trade association ('Profesni sdruzeni firem z oboru IT informacnich technologii a elektronickych komunikaci') publishing a member list of roughly 60 companies with logos, an Aktuality stream, a 'V mediich' clippings section, working groups and sector statistics drawn from the Czech Statistical Office. This is the cheapest way to complete the vendor actor map beyond the ten seed names and to pick up the sector-level aggregates that contextualise individual vendor wins.

source_name: KPKB ČR – Komora podniků komerční bezpečnosti ČR (kpkbcr.cz) and allied security associations
why_relevant: Sector chamber for commercial security businesses (founded January 1993) with corporate and individual member directories, a magazine, guard-qualification exam material and downloadable organisational documents. Cash-in-transit in Czechia is legally and operationally part of the commercial-security industry, so this chamber and its partner bodies (Česká komora služeb ochrany majetku a osob, Grémium Alarm, Česká asociace bezpečnostních manažerů, Hospodářská komora ČR) are the route to enumerating smaller and regional CIT/valuables-transport firms that no financial-sector list captures. Note: the partner page did not list Loomis/Brink's/Securitas, so membership coverage of the large CIT players is unconfirmed.

source_name: MarketScreener (English aggregator of listed-bank news)
why_relevant: Aggregates company news, regulatory filings and analyst commentary per listed issuer in English, including Prague Stock Exchange-listed banks. Valuable as a pointer layer: a per-company news timeline that reveals which English outlets and which primary disclosures exist for a given Czech bank, without having to guess each issuer's IR page.

source_name: Max banka a.s. – legacy mandatory-disclosure archive (now a CREDITAS product line)
why_relevant: Max banka no longer exists as an independent bank — it merged into Banka CREDITAS and maxbanka.eu now presents itself as the 'Max' product line of Banka CREDITAS. The page nonetheless still serves a complete historical archive: annual reports 2010–2023, ČBA-format quarterly filings 2021–2024 (latest observed 30 Sep 2024), and disclosure annexes back to 2015. This is a closing time-window: valuable to harvest now for the pre-merger baseline of a bank that also carries the earlier Expobank CZ lineage, and likely to be retired. Its news section also documented the merger mechanics (bank code 4000 to 2250, instant payments introduction).

source_name: Mediář – daily Czech media/marketing news and PR agency index
why_relevant: Independent daily (News Media s.r.o., editor Ondřej Aust) with dedicated /pr/ and /agentury/ sections listing dozens of Czech PR agencies. Snowballing the agency index identifies the intermediaries that write and place bank and payments press releases — a route to announcements that never reach a corporate newsroom, and a way to anticipate campaigns.

source_name: Zlatá koruna
why_relevant: A 22-year-old Czech financial-product award and catalogue operated by pdMEDIA s.r.o. Two things make it a pointer of unusual value for this cell: a searchable comparison catalogue of 'more than 700 financial products' spanning accounts, mortgages, loans, insurance, funds and business services (/financni-produkty), and an award archive at /soutez with published results for 2009-2025. The award archive is effectively a longitudinal, year-by-year map of which Czech banks fielded which products and which were judged innovative - a ready-made time series for tracking product-innovation posture per institution, and a snowball surface that names smaller banks, fintechs and product lines that mainstream coverage skips. Also runs /zpravy and /diskuse (including a 'vision for banking' forum).
